headline: Shares of hard drive makers Seagate and Western Digital fell by roughly 10% to 13% in trading on Friday after a report that rival Toshiba plans to double its hard drive production capacity for AI data centres.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the headline's talk of an easing shortage overstates a one-day share move on a reported plan that is not yet built.
importance_line: It shows how quickly these two stocks, up roughly 240% and 170% this year before the fall, can drop on news of new competition, which matters to their investors and to data centres that buy their drives, but Toshiba's plan is still only a report, runs to 2027, and Toshiba currently holds just over 10% of the market.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Seagate and Western Digital shares fell sharply on Friday 2 October after Nikkei reported that Toshiba plans to spend about 60 billion yen (around $400 million) to double its hard drive production capacity by financial year 2027. What is new is the market reaction: Yahoo Finance says investors worry that Toshiba, which has just over 10% of the market and wants 30%, could take market share and put pressure on prices at the AI data centres that buy these drives.
notes: Original outlet Barron's (url https://www.barrons.com/articles/seagate-stock-western-digital-ai-data-centers-ab47e2a8) was blocked (401), so the entry is written from and credits Yahoo Finance (Proactive), which reports the Nikkei story. Follow-up of the 2 Oct edition item C08-05 (Nikkei Asia, Toshiba hard drive doubling). Toshiba's plan is Nikkei's report, not confirmed by Toshiba in the text read.
